blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Lawmakers should consider passing legislation against undersea cable sabotage to ensure that authorities have the legal toolkit to punish potential disruptors, a former National Security Council official said on Tuesday, amid concerns that subsea cable damage could be a tool of coercion. Jonathan Malaya, who now leads the University of the Philippines Center for International Strategic Studies, said policy conversations must address how to safeguard critical subsea cables across the archipelago. “These are conversations that should be done now, before some state-sponsored shadow fleet utilizes the subsea cables as a form of coercion,” he said at the Manila […]...
